hyperedges.label: End-to-end local onboarding flow: fork/clone the repo, set up the frontend, optionally run via Docker, and pair with the separate backend repo
Automated code-quality enforcement pipeline spanning commit-time hooks, editor standards, and PR title linting
Pattern of documenting duplicate/competing implementations in known-issues.md and instructing coding agents to ask rather than silently pick one
Layer B (integrations/ApiConnector/getClubs/getEvents) exists but is unused, and its intended consumer pages fall back to hardcoded data instead
Login-state is checked three inconsistent ways across the app (Redux selector, cookie+Redux, and a second unrelated cookie), consumed by the route guard and Navbar

The 'two implementations exist, ask before editing' meta-pattern this codebase repeatedly exhibits: duplicate create-event components, duplicate profile pages, duplicate profile-edit modals, duplicate auth buttons, and duplicate validation systems
Two independently-implemented create-event flows sharing a similar name
hyperedges.description: CreateEvent (shared, structurally copied from ProfileUpdate, and its validateForm() actually calls updateUserProfile/PATCH /user/update instead of creating an event) versus CreateEvents (private, MUI-based, wired through useEvent to the real POST /events/create endpoint but unreachable from any page). The spec explicitly instructs asking which one a request means.

hyperedges.label: Two profile-edit modals reached through inconsistent trigger conditions
hyperedges.description: ProfileCompletion and ProfileUpdate are near-duplicate forms. Dashboard.jsx's Edit Profile button opens ProfileUpdate, while Profile.jsx's own Edit-profile button opens ProfileCompletion instead. Separately, Profile.jsx and Dashboard.jsx use different conditions (checkMissingFields vs hasCompletedProfile flag) to decide whether to auto-show the completion modal, so a user could satisfy one check and not the other.

hyperedges.label: Two overlapping public 'view a profile' pages, one of them unrouted
hyperedges.description: Profile.jsx (routed at /user/:userName and /club/:userName, fetches via clubEndpoints.details, linked to from ClubCard) and UserProfile.jsx (visually more developed, fetches via userEndpoints.details, but has no route in routesConfig.jsx and relies on a cookie that's never set) both implement a 'view someone's profile' page; the spec treats UserProfile.jsx as a work-in-progress replacement rather than an active page.
